title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: foresight of sanctity not cause — decree precedes foresight
pass_a_gloss: In the places alleged it is not said that God elected or predestinated certain men unto glory because he foresaw that they would be conformed to the image of Christ, that is, holy and good, but it is said that he elected those whom he foreknew, and predestinated them that they might be made conformed, or elected them unto sanctification. Therefore foreknowledge of future holiness was not the cause of predestination, but predestination the cause of the foresight of holiness. For God foresees no saving and spiritual good in men except what he himself works in them; he works no good except what he has decreed to work. Therefore the decree of working grace and holiness, which is included in predestination, always precedes the foresight of grace and holiness understood as present in men.
pass_b_english: Reply: those texts do not say God elected or predestined certain people to glory because he foresaw they would be conformed to Christ's image — holy and good. They say he elected those he foreknew, and predestined them to become conformed, or elected them unto sanctification. So foresight of future holiness was not the cause of predestination; predestination was the cause of the holiness foreseen. God foresees no saving spiritual good in people except what he himself works in them; he works none except what he decreed to work. The decree to work grace and holiness — already wrapped into predestination — always comes before any foresight of grace and holiness as in them.
source_text: In locis allegatis non dicitur Deus elegisse aut praedestinasse certos homines ad gloriam quia praescivit eos fore conformes imagini Christi, id est, sanctos & bonos, sed dicitur eos elegisse quos praescivit, atque praedestinasse ut conformes fierent, vel elegisse in sanctificationem. Praescientia igitur futurae sanctitatis non fuit causa praedestinationis, sed praedestinatio causa praevisae sanctitatis. Deus enim nullum bonum salutiferum & spirituale in hominibus praevidet, nisi quod ipse in illis operatur; nullum bonum operatur, nisi quod decrevit operari. Decretum igitur operandi gratiam & sanctitatem, quod in praedestinatione includitur, semper praecedit praevisionem gratiae & sanctitatis, quae hominibus inesse intelligitur.
